text.p: European Commissioner Hans van den Broek said on Wednesday that the Lithuanian government was pursuing bold reforms needed to complete the country's transition to a market economy.
The commissioner arrived in Lithuania on Wednesday for a two-day official visit.

"The new government...has taken very bold steps in the direction of further economic reform, including further privatisation and restructuring of industries," Van den Broek told Reuters after meeting with President Algirdas Brazauskas.
"All of those things are very important conditions to be successful in operating in a market economy without borders," he added.
The new government headed by Gediminas Vagnorius has committed itself to completing the privatisation process launched during his first term in office in 1991-1992.
It has drawn up a list of key state enterprises in the energy, transport and communications sectors which are to be sold.
Joining the European Union is one of Lithuania's central foreign policy goals.
